prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1141; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two witnesses along with photos from the scene. Both witnesses and the other driver describe the accident the same way, and the claimant is confirmed as being in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Inspected the insured vehicle and the damage matches the impact described by all parties. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 4: Medical records show the wrist fracture was treated along a usual course, with care tapering off as the patient improved. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash, since prior records show a small strain in the same area years ago that healed fully.

Entry 5: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far. Requested the full prior medical history through counsel to help determine causation.

Entry 6: Next step is to obtain an independent medical review of the records before making any decision on the bodily injury portion of the claim. Reserve remains open pending that review.
